ANSWER: The guard is implemented across two files:

**`pkg/okf/provenance.go`**
- `IsHumanIdentity(id string) bool` — the canonical predicate; returns `true` if the actor identifier equals `"human"` or starts with `"human:"` / `"human/"` (case-insensitive).
- `ensureNoForgedHumanVerification(fullPath string, c *Concept, actor string, isNew bool) error` — the enforcement function. If `actor` is not a human identity, it reads the existing concept on disk, then rejects any `Verified` entry whose `By` field satisfies `IsHumanIdentity` and was not already present in the saved file. For a brand-new concept (`isNew == true`) every such entry is rejected outright.
- `recordedVerifications(fullPath string) map[Verified]bool` — helper that loads the on-disk copy to build the set of already-persisted verifications.

**`pkg/okf/mutate.go`**
- `saveConceptLocked` (line ~476) — the single internal write path for all concept mutations. It calls `ensureNoForgedHumanVerification(fullPath, c, actor, opts.IsNew)` before any file is written, so the concept is never persisted if the check fires.

The MCP server (`pkg/okf/mcp.go`) hardcodes `Actor: "agent/mcp"` in every write handler (`okf_create`, `okf_update`, `okf_relate`). Because `"agent/mcp"` does not satisfy `IsHumanIdentity`, any attempt by the MCP agent to include a human `Verified` entry is caught by `ensureNoForgedHumanVerification` inside `saveConceptLocked` and returns an error before the file is touched.

CONFIDENCE: high
